At p=1 every new node brings one edge and the graph is a tree of 7 edges; the mixed p=0.5 gives 13 edges; at p=0 every new node brings three, for 15." width="100%"} Grows a graph from a star on `max(m1, m2) + 1` nodes. Each new node attaches with `m1` edges with probability `p` and with `m2` edges otherwise, linking to distinct existing nodes chosen with probability proportional to their degree. Mixing the two attachment sizes gives a degree distribution between those of the two pure Barabási-Albert models, and lets the average degree be any value between `2 * m1` and `2 * m2`. With `p=1` (or `p=0`) this is the Barabási-Albert model with `m1` (or `m2`) edges per node, started from a star on `m1 + 1` (or `m2 + 1`) nodes rather than the clique used by `add_pa_graph()`. The process follows NetworkX's `dual_barabasi_albert_graph()`. In a directed graph the star's edges point from its center to its leaves, and every later edge points from the new node to the node it attached to, as in `add_pa_graph()`. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Dual Barabási-Albert graphs are useful for: - scale-free graphs with a non-integer average degree, e.g. to match an observed network - modeling growth in which newcomers differ in how many links they bring - comparing against `add_pa_graph()` as the attachment mix varies ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. Must be greater than both `m1=` and `m2=`. [m1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of edges a new node makes with probability `p=`. Must be at least `1`. [m2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of edges a new node makes otherwise. Must be at least `1`. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of attaching with `m1=` edges, between `0` and `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `m1=` or `m2=` is less than `1` or not less than `n=`, or `p=` is not between `0` and `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} New nodes bring one edge or four, with equal chance: ::: {#34bf1055 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_dual_barabasi_albert_graph(n=200, m1=1, m2=4, p=0.5, seed=6) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (200, 511) ``` ::: ::: The average degree slides between `2 * m2` and `2 * m1` as `p=` goes from `0` to `1`: ::: {#6287c970 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ round( ec.Graph() .add_dual_barabasi_albert_graph(n=200, m1=1, m2=4, p=p, seed=6) .average_degree(), 2, ) for p in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [7.84, 5.11, 1.99] ``` ::: :::
